set: The Last Five Weapons, In Space This Time
lede:
You kept full_auto_20, and then said the thing that matters more than the verdict: “these should be spaceship and space opera themed you know?” They should. Twenty takes came back as a WWII factory — brass, deck grating, a gloved hand, oily steel — and the reason is that I never told the generator where any of it was.

The answer was already written down, in this repo, unread

docs/design-doc.md has a visual-direction section I had not opened before writing a single card prompt. It says, in its own words:

“The void is never flat black. Deep indigo-to-black dithered gradients with nebula wash coloured per region — Korvan space rusty amber.”

“Objects are genuinely lush. Weathered plating, stencilled hull numbers, decals, lit viewports with tiny interior detail. Spend the pixel budget here.”

“Warm/cold survives as lighting logic… objects are richly coloured but coldly lit, with warm rim light from your own reactor and engines. Your heat glow reads because it is the only self-emitted warmth in frame.”

Industrial was never the problem — the doc names the tone “lush-cold industrial” against Cobalt Core's cartoon brightness. Industry on Earth was. Every brief now carries a the world line saying so, and it is the same line on every card because it is house style, not a per-card decision.

Your call on full_auto_20: it is installed, and it is the most factory-ish of the eleven that ship. Say the word and it goes back through with a viewport in it.

cards.on: a heavy round it is lifting up out of the deck onto a rack
cards.moment: the round clears the hatch and swings onto the rack, chain taut and taking the weight. Nothing has fired. This card is the feed, not the shot.
cards.scale: the magazine is a ship compartment: a low ceiling with conduit runs, a rack of identical rounds receding, and a lit viewport or an open bay door in the wall with the void beyond it. The room says starship; the round says heavy.
cards.avoid: a muzzle flash, and any word from the banned list — no 'gun', no 'weapon', no 'shell', no 'hull', no 'vessel'. Say hoist, chain, rack, round, magazine, conduit.

cards.on: the flank of an enemy starship
cards.moment: the walk seen from the target's side: hits marching across weathered plating with stencilled numbers on it, the newest white-hot and throwing debris, the older ones behind cooling to dark scabs. The impacts are the only warm light in frame.
cards.scale: the plating carries a stencilled hull number and a lit viewport or two, so the surface being chewed is unmistakably a ship rather than a wall — and the nebula wash sits behind the curve of it.
cards.avoid: any weapon in frame at all — Drumfire's other card can have the machine, this one is what the machine does to somebody. No banned words.

cards.on: a starship it has not hit yet
cards.moment: the shard throws a surveyed line across the void to a mark sitting on an intact ship. The violence is entirely in the future tense, and that is what separates it from every other attack card in the game.
cards.scale: the shard is close and the ship is far and small, with a nebula wash between them carrying the distance. The precursor violet of the shard against the amber of Korvan space is the whole colour story.
cards.avoid: a hand holding a crystal — the shard is the actor, not a prop. Do not let the shard elongate into something that reads as a missile; that happened twice. No banned words.

cards.actor: a standing wave off the Singing Core
cards.on: a bulkhead coming apart along its seams
cards.moment: the plate failing where the wave nodes sit: rivets shearing in a regular repeating pattern, metal parting along lines too evenly spaced to be blast damage. Two big hits, two nodes. Nothing burns — it comes apart.
cards.scale: a compartment interior with the void visible through the split that is opening, so the failure reads as a breach rather than as a wall cracking. Cold light, precursor violet at the fracture.
cards.avoid: fire and explosion of any kind — one take put an open flame in it and the module does not burn things. No warm light except the resonance itself. No banned words.

cards.on: a dead starship it is opening
cards.moment: the flame biting into cold plating, cutting a slot rather than a hole, slag running off the bottom edge of the cut. Salvage work — the module is 'meant for hulls that are already dead' — so the picture should look like a job, not a fight.
cards.scale: the derelict fills the frame and runs out of it, dark and unlit, with dead viewports and a stencilled number. The torch is the only light source in the picture and the void is behind the wreck.
cards.avoid: reading as the Mining Laser's Cutting Beam, which already ships — that one is a beam at range, this is a flame in contact. No banned words; say plating, derelict, slag, arc.
